chunks: They say: "The Most Merciful has taken a son."

key_terms.الرَّحْمَٰنُ: The Most Merciful (a specific divine name)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say when disbelievers claim God has a son?
ai.summary: In Shia tafsir, this verse is often contextualized within the broader critique of anthropomorphic conceptions of divinity, where 'sonship' (ibn) symbolizes a created, dependent status rather than literal biological procreation. The verse serves as a prelude to the Quranic assertion of God's absolute transcendence (tanzih), refuting the notion that the Creator could be subject to the limitations of creation. This theological stance aligns with the Shia emphasis on the unique, uncreated nature of the Divine Essence, distinct from any created entity, including the Ahl al-Bayt who are revered but not deified.
